initial.title: [v0.92][C-SDLC v2] Remove claims from the lifecycle
initial.goal: Complete the deletion of claims as a C-SDLC v2 lifecycle concept while preserving one atomic issue-to-branch/worktree binding.
initial.required_outcome: No active schema, command, gate, skill, or current operator document requires claim state; current claim-bearing legacy-format records normalize into canonical topology, historical evidence remains immutable, and the full lifecycle works from branch/worktree binding alone.
authority_boundary: PR body must use Closes danielbaustin/agent-design-language#5881
This is split issue/code publication authority, not repository cutover or issue migration
Claim-specific decoding is temporary only for verified current-record normalization and must be deleted before completion
operator_constraints: No wrappers, retries, or renamed claim abstraction
Execute after #5895 and #5883 and rebase shared operator surfaces
Prefer evidence over replacement code for already-satisfied acceptance
initial.task_boundary: Remove residual active claim lifecycle authority and prove canonical branch/worktree ownership end to end.
deliverables: Verified one-time current-record normalization with claim-specific production logic deleted afterward
Atomic, concurrent, and interrupted-bind recovery proof
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: No active request or canonical schema contains claim, claim_id, protected_paths, lease, or heartbeat fields
AC-2: No operator command requires claim acquisition, refresh, recovery, release, revoke, rehome, or amend
AC-3: Existing current issue records normalize without manual claim repair while preserving branch/worktree topology and audit truth, and no claim-specific production decoder remains afterward
AC-4: Concurrent binds for one issue cannot produce two authoritative worktrees
AC-5: Different issues can bind and execute concurrently without path reservations
AC-6: Review, publication, finish, and cleanup pass from bound topology alone
AC-7: Focused Rust tests and owner validation pass
AC-8: Claim-specific active code, schemas, fixtures, docs, and binaries are deleted rather than wrapped
AC-9: An interrupted bind transaction recovers to one valid authoritative topology without claim state or partial records
non_goals: Weaken review, validation, publication, finish, or cleanup
Replace claims with another reservation ledger
initial.plan_summary: Rebase after the two narrow deletion issues, classify claim surfaces, normalize current records once, delete all claim-specific production logic, and prove crash-safe binding plus the full lifecycle from branch/worktree topology.

steps.action: Rebase after #5895 and #5883 and classify all claim-related occurrences as active authority, temporary current-record normalization, historical evidence, or unrelated language.
Delete residual active claim fields, operations, gates, schemas, fixtures, skills, and current operator guidance without adding compatibility routes.
Normalize current claim-bearing records through a verified one-time path, preserve topology and audit truth, then delete the claim-specific decoder and structs.
Run focused atomic/idempotent/concurrent/interrupted bind and claim-free review, publication, finish, and cleanup validation.

invariants: One authoritative branch/worktree pair per issue
Exact-head review and terminal authority unchanged
risks: Deleting temporary normalization support before current records normalize
Failing to delete claim-specific production logic after normalization
Treating ordinary evidence claims as lifecycle claims
Leaving an installed skill or schema route stale
stop_conditions: A proposed change weakens exact-head review or terminal authority
Current claim-bearing legacy-format records cannot be normalized without destructive rewriting
The issue would require a new compatibility wrapper
Shared #5895 or #5883 changes have not settled

validation_lanes.proof_role: Prove canonical requests, records, schemas, and CLI surfaces contain no claim lifecycle state.
Prove current claim-bearing records normalize once with topology and audit truth preserved, then prove claim-specific production structs and logic are absent.
Prove atomic/idempotent same-issue bind, different-issue concurrency, and interrupted-bind recovery without claims.
Prove exact-head review, qualified cross-repository publication, finish, and cleanup derive authority from bound topology without claim IDs.
Prove current skills, policies, and runbooks use only claim-free binding while historical evidence remains untouched.

initial.failure_policy: Fail closed on duplicate authoritative topology, active claim state, manual historical-record repair, weakened review/finish truth, compatibility routing, or historical evidence mutation.
review_prompts: Does any public schema, binary, installed skill, or current doc still require lifecycle claim state?
Did verified one-time normalization preserve current-record topology and audit truth, followed by deletion of every claim-specific production decoder, struct, and compatibility path?
Do same-issue, different-issue, and interrupted-bind tests prove the required concurrency and crash-recovery semantics?
Does the full review-to-cleanup path derive authority only from issue topology and live GitHub state?
initial.review_scope: Residual claim deletion, verified one-time current-record normalization followed by complete claim-specific production logic deletion, topology concurrency and crash recovery, and claim-free lifecycle proof only.
